The '''2021–22 season''' was '''[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool Football Club]]''''s [[List of Liverpool F.C. seasons|130th season]] in existence and their 60th consecutive season in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of [[Football in England|English football]]. Liverpool were on course to winning a unique quadruple, as they won a record-breaking ninth [[2021–22 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and the [[2021–22 FA Cup|FA Cup]], beating [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on penalties in both finals. However, they lost the [[2021–22 Premier League|Premier League]] title by one point to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], and – in a repeat of the [[2018 UEFA Champions League final|2018 final]] – lost the [[2022 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League final]] to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. This was the first season since [[2015–16 Liverpool F.C. season|2015–16]] without [[Georginio Wijnaldum]], who departed to [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] and the first since [[2017–18 Liverpool F.C. season|2017–18]] without [[Xherdan Shaqiri]], who departed to [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]].

==Season overview==
Liverpool excelled in both the [[FA Cup]] and [[EFL Cup]], beating [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in both finals on penalties after both matches ended in goalless draws. On the final day of the season, Liverpool faced [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] at [[Anfield]], while their title challengers Manchester City faced [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] at the [[City of Manchester Stadium|Etihad Stadium]]. Liverpool found themselves 0–1 down early in the match, however, City were also a goal down to Villa. [[Sadio Mané]] levelled the scoreline for Liverpool, and their title hopes were kept alive by the fact that City were now 0–2 down. However, City went on to score three goals in five minutes to take the lead and, despite [[Mohamed Salah]] and [[Andy Robertson]] scoring two late goals to beat Wolves 3–1, it was not enough and the Reds were pipped to the title by a point. Meanwhile in the [[UEFA Champions League]], despite being drawn in a group with [[Atlético Madrid]], [[AC Milan]] and [[FC Porto|Porto]], Liverpool made history by becoming the first English club to win all six group stage matches. They advanced all the way to [[2022 UEFA Champions League final|the final]] where they took on [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], as they had done [[2018 UEFA Champions League final|four years earlier]]. In [[Paris]], the same city in which the Reds won the European Cup against Madrid in [[1981 European Cup final|1981]], they lost 0–1 as [[Vinícius Júnior]] scored the only goal of the game for ''Los Blancos''.

==Pre-season and friendlies==
On 12 July 2021, Liverpool announced that they would play four friendlies as part of a pre-season training camp in [[Austria]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool confirm pre-season fixtures in Austria |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/437657-liverpool-confirm-pre-season-fixtures-in-austria |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=12 July 2021}}</ref> On 19 July, they stated that they would complete their pre-season campaign with two home friendlies.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool to play two pre-season friendlies at Anfield |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/438251-liverpool-to-play-two-pre-season-friendlies-at-anfield |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=19 July 2021}}</ref> On 29 July, the Reds confirmed that they would face [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]] in two sixty-minute matches as part of a training camp in [[France]] in between the previously announced engagements.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool to contest Bologna friendlies in Evian |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/439310-liverpool-to-contest-bologna-friendlies-in-evian |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=29 July 2021}}</ref>

====Knockout phase====
{{main|2021–22 UEFA Champions League knockout phase}}
=====Round of 16=====
The draw for the round of 16 took place on 13 December 2021 at [[UEFA]]'s headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland. Liverpool were drawn against reigning [[2020–21 Serie A|Serie A]] champions [[Inter Milan]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0265-115e77805e06-3dbc1740a323-1000/ |title=2021/22 UEFA Champions League: all you need to know |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=19 January 2021 |access-date=19 January 2021}}</ref>

=====Final=====
{{main|2022 UEFA Champions League final}}

The final was held on 28 May 2022 in [[Paris]], with Liverpool facing 13-time winners [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. This was Liverpool's tenth European Cup final, the most of any English club, and third in five years; it was a rematch of the [[2018 UEFA Champions League final|2018 final]], which Liverpool lost 1–3.
